honest_scope: The two commits the reviewing engine is built from. They are PINNED, which is what makes the reviewer independent of the candidate; they are not APPROVED, because `GET /releases` returns [] and operator prerequisite 14 is unrecorded. With no artifact digest and no release tag, `engine.provenance_of` labels this REBUILT_FROM_PINNED_SOURCE_TEST_ONLY, and `assert_provenance_permits` refuses it for any run that spends money. A dry run may use it.
sha_fields_are_git_commit_ids: The two `*_sha` values below are 40-hex git commit ids, not credentials. An entropy detector cannot tell the difference, which is the correct default, so they carry an audited entry in `.secrets.baseline` — JSON has no comment syntax, so an inline `pragma: allowlist secret` is not available here.
operator_action_required: Build the artifact from these two commits, record its sha256 here, and cut a release tag. Only then does provenance_of return APPROVED_RELEASE and only then may a provider-backed run proceed.

The engine source deliberately LAGS the candidate. A pull request that changes scripts/verifier is reviewed by the engine pinned here, not by its own edited code; picking up that change means merging it first and then re-pinning.
